summary: Announcement of a Network Data Management meeting at MITRE on February 23 and 24, 1972. It aimed to hear about network data applications and to work toward a specification for a network data management protocol, using written proposals.

eli5.summary: A call to a meeting to talk about how computers on a network could manage and share data, and to start writing the rules.

subtitle: An announcement of a February 1972 working meeting to design network protocols for data management.

tldr.problem: The ARPA network needed a standardized way for systems to share data, and the community had recognized the need but lacked a concrete design.
tldr.mechanism: MITRE hosted a two-day working meeting in February 1972 with presentations from various organizations about their data management needs, followed by a working session to draft a network data management protocol.
tldr.outcome: The meeting brought together stakeholders to coordinate on a specification for a third-level protocol for data sharing, building on earlier RFC-146 recommendations.

today: RFC 291 documents a crucial working session in the history of ARPA network protocols, January 1972. It shows the community transitioning from identifying needs to systematic protocol design.

sections.title: The Meeting Purpose
sections.content:
MITRE Corporation announced a Network Data Management Meeting to be held February 23-24, 1972. The meeting was a follow-on from an earlier data management session in August 1971 and served two main objectives.

First, it would hear presentations from various organizations about their needs and experience with network data facilities, focusing on real-world applications. Second, it would work toward a specification for a network data management protocol, a third-level protocol enabling sites to share data reliably.
sections.eli5: People from different organizations would meet to talk about what they needed for sharing data, and then write down the rules for how to do it.

sections.title: Speakers and Applications
sections.content:
The meeting featured speakers discussing diverse data management applications. Captain Roger Moore discussed medical file sharing for the U.S. Army R&D Command. The National Medical Board of Examiners needed to access test results from testing centers across the country. Hughes Aircraft shared their perspective on practical applications in their operations.

Dick Watson from SRI-NIC discussed the possibility of distributing parts of the Network Information Center itself across the network. These presentations grounded the protocol design discussion in actual user requirements and use cases.
sections.eli5: Speakers explained what their organizations needed, like hospitals that wanted to share patient test results across the country.

sections.title: Protocol Design Effort
sections.content:
The second half of the meeting was reserved as a working session for designing the protocol itself. D. B. McKay intended to circulate draft proposals before the meeting to stimulate discussion. He encouraged anyone interested in submitting a protocol design to do so.

Attendance was limited to those who had participated in previous data management meetings, with D. B. McKay managing registrations. Reservations required contacting Mrs. Madeline Cornell at MITRE. The protocol design effort aimed to achieve the objectives outlined in RFC-146 for a network data facility.
sections.eli5: Engineers met to draft a protocol specification that all computers could use to share data with each other.
